context_title: The user wants to see the directory that CONTAINS the /home folder, i.e., the root / directory.

entries.query: The user wants to see the directory that CONTAINS the /home folder, i.e., the root / directory.
entries.answer:
A root directory, which is /, is the toplevel directory that contains /home and the rest of the filesystem hierarchy. In other words, /home is a subdirectory inside /, not the other way around.[1][2][3]

 What it looks like

A typical Linuxstyle layout is:

text
/
├── home
├── root
├── etc
├── usr
├── var
└── ...


That means if you want the directory that contains /home, you want /.[3][1]

 How to view it

In a terminal, you can list the root directory with:

bash
ls /


If you want, I can also show the difference between /, /home, and ~ in one short example.
